stars.label: Could a machine be aware?
stars.title: Could a machine be aware?
stars.body: Nobody agrees on what would show it. Some think awareness needs a living body, some think the right pattern of information would do, and some think the question is badly posed.

stars.label: Is the self a story?
stars.title: Is the self a story we tell?
stars.body: We piece together who we are from memory and the tales others tell about us. Whether anything lies underneath is argued by philosophers and by several religious traditions in different ways.

stars.label: Do we choose?
stars.title: Do we choose what we do?
stars.body: The feeling of choosing is strong. How it fits with laws of nature, or with what the brain does before we notice, is the live part of the question.

stars.label: Do animals have minds?
stars.title: Which animals have minds like ours?
stars.body: Crows, octopuses, elephants and bees surprise people who study them. Where awareness starts is open, and the answer changes what we think we owe them.

stars.label: Can all be said in any language?
stars.title: Can anything be said in any language?
stars.body: Translators say that nearly anything can be explained, though not always briefly or with the same feeling. Whether some thoughts belong to one language is the open part.

stars.label: What do we lose with a language?
stars.title: What is lost when a language falls silent?
stars.body: A language holds names for plants, songs, jokes and ways of being polite. Communities and linguists are still working out what can be kept in a recording and what needs a living speaker.

stars.label: Where does meaning live?
stars.title: Where does meaning live?
stars.body: In the speaker’s mind, in the community’s habits or in the link to the world? Each answer fits some cases and fails others.

stars.label: Why do the same tales recur?
stars.title: Why do similar tales turn up in different places?
stars.body: Travel and trade carry stories along. Shared human concerns may bring similar tales out of different places. Scholars weigh both, case by case.

stars.label: Who decides what is literature?
stars.title: Who decides what counts as literature?
stars.body: Schools, publishers, prizes and readers all shape which writing is kept. Whose writing was left out, and in which language, is a question many communities now ask.

stars.label: Can stories be shared with care?
stars.title: How can a community’s stories be shared with care?
stars.body: Some stories are meant for anyone. Some belong to a family, a clan or a season. Asking who may tell a story, and how, is part of reading it well.

stars.label: How did life begin?
stars.title: How did life begin?
stars.body: Chemistry became biology at least once, probably within the first billion years. Which steps came in which order is still unknown.

stars.label: Is there life elsewhere?
stars.title: Is there life elsewhere?
stars.body: No one has found any yet. Telescopes can now read the air of distant planets, and each reading adds a clue to the search.

stars.label: What is a living thing?
stars.title: What counts as a living thing?
stars.body: Cells, viruses, flames and programs that copy themselves sit at different points of any definition. The edge says something about what we mean.

stars.label: Why do we age?
stars.title: Why do living things age?
stars.body: Biologists have several accounts of why evolution lets bodies wear out. Whether aging can be slowed, and whether it should be, is a question for ethics as well as biology.

stars.label: How should we act on climate?
stars.title: How should societies act on climate?
stars.body: The measurements are clear about the warming. What to do, how fast and who pays are matters of values and politics where reasonable people differ.

stars.label: Should this age be named?
stars.title: Should the present be named as an age of people?
stars.body: The name Anthropocene is used widely and rejected by some scientists and critics. The argument is about evidence and also about who the name includes.

stars.label: Can we feel deep time?
stars.title: Can a person feel deep time?
stars.body: Millions of years pass beyond any memory or story. Maps, rock layers and walks along a timeline all try to help.

stars.label: What makes people trust?
stars.title: What makes people trust each other?
stars.body: Shared rules, repeated dealings, a common story and courts all help. It is not yet clear how much of it a large online world can rebuild.

stars.label: Who should hold the commons?
stars.title: Who should look after what belongs to everyone?
stars.body: Villages, states, markets and online communities have all tried. What worked depended on the people, the place and the rules they made together.

stars.label: Can power check itself?
stars.title: Can power be checked from inside?
stars.body: Courts, elections, a free press and an opposition try to. Gödel’s worry, and many histories, suggest the check has to come from somewhere the power does not fully control.

stars.label: What is fair?
stars.title: What is a fair share?
stars.body: Equal shares, shares by effort and shares by need each sound right in some cases. Societies mix them, and the mix is the argument.

stars.label: Do values differ everywhere?
stars.title: Are values different everywhere?
stars.body: Customs vary widely. Some values, such as care for the young, turn up in nearly every society. How much is shared and how much is local is still studied.

stars.label: What do we owe the unborn?
stars.title: What do we owe people who are not yet born?
stars.body: Climate, waste and new technology shape their lives and they cannot speak. Several traditions teach thinking many generations ahead.

stars.label: What gives life meaning?
stars.title: What gives a life meaning?
stars.body: Faith, love, work, understanding and making something are named across traditions and by people with no tradition. The answers live side by side here.

stars.label: Do animals have rights?
stars.title: Do animals have rights?
stars.body: Views range from welfare rules to full rights, and many traditions teach kinship with other species. The answer depends partly on what animals feel.

stars.label: Who should decide about AI?
stars.title: Who should decide how AI is built and used?
stars.body: Companies, governments, researchers and the public all have a stake. Who decides, and who can say no, is part of the technology.

stars.label: Can an AI check its own safety?
stars.title: Can an AI check that its successor is safe?
stars.body: A system that wants to trust a stronger version of itself meets a limit like Löb’s. Humans and other checks may be part of the answer.

stars.label: What does the internet change?
stars.title: What does the internet change in how we think?
stars.body: Everything is a few taps away, and so is everyone. Attention, memory and trust have all been argued to shift, and the evidence is still being gathered.

stars.label: Which tools change us most?
stars.title: Which tools changed people most?
stars.body: Writing, printing, clocks and screens are common answers. Each changed what was worth remembering.

stars.label: What is beauty for?
stars.title: What is beauty for?
stars.body: Some say it guides us to what is good for us, some say it is a pleasure with no purpose, some say it is made by habit and place. Each has examples.

stars.label: Who owns a style or a song?
stars.title: Who owns a style, a tune or a story?
stars.body: Artists learn by copying, and some works belong to a community more than to a person. Law draws lines that many people feel are in the wrong place.

stars.label: Is art a language?
stars.title: Is art a language?
stars.body: Music, dance and painting carry meaning without words. Whether they have a grammar of their own is something scholars of each art keep asking.

stars.label: Can a machine make art?
stars.title: Can a machine make art?
stars.body: Programs now produce pictures and tunes that people enjoy. Whether art needs someone who means something by it is the heart of the question.

stars.label: Can traditions understand?
stars.title: Can people of different traditions understand each other?
stars.body: Dialogue works best when each side describes itself and listens before replying. What can be shared and what has to stay different is part of the conversation.

stars.label: How far does belief freedom reach?
stars.title: How far does freedom of belief reach?
stars.body: It covers holding a belief and changing it. How far it covers acting on it, teaching it or leaving it is argued in courts around the world.

stars.label: Can science and religion meet?
stars.title: Can science and religion meet?
stars.body: Some say they answer separate questions, some find tension, and some find help. Careful people hold each view.

stars.label: What do rituals do?
stars.title: What do rituals do for people?
stars.body: They mark change, hold a group together and calm the person. Why repeating a set of acts has these effects is still studied.

stars.label: What can a text carry across ages?
stars.title: What can a text carry across the ages?
stars.body: Words change, readers change and translators choose. Traditions keep texts alive by reading, chanting and arguing over them again and again.

stars.label: What do mystics report?
stars.title: What do people report from mystical experience?
stars.body: Accounts from many traditions describe a sense of unity or of presence. Believers and researchers read them in different ways, and the reports are worth reading side by side.

stars.label: How does a people hold knowledge?
stars.title: How does a people hold what it knows?
stars.body: Songs, stories, crafts, seasons and elders carry knowledge in many communities. Writing may be added, and it changes some things.

stars.label: Who keeps a people’s objects?
stars.title: Who should keep the objects of a people?
stars.body: Museums, source communities and states have different claims. Many agreements now exist, and each case is a conversation.

stars.label: How does each people read the sky?
stars.title: How does each people read the sky?
stars.body: Every culture has watched the sky and made it part of its life: planting, travel, stories, ceremony. The readings differ and can be learned side by side.

stars.label: Can a culture change and last?
stars.title: Can a culture change and still be itself?
stars.body: Cultures have always changed through contact. What a people wishes to keep, and who decides, shapes the answer.

stars.label: What does food carry?
stars.title: What does a meal carry?
stars.body: A meal can carry memory, belonging, belief and welcome. Recipes travel and change, and some keep a place alive far from home.

stars.label: Whose voice is missing?
stars.title: Whose voice is missing from the map?
stars.body: Any map of ideas leaves people out: languages, traditions and peoples. Anyone can add or correct what is here, and people from each tradition and culture are invited to speak for themselves.
